newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Saudi deal to cover 40 pct Petrogal crude needs.
newsitem.headline: Saudi deal to cover 40 pct Petrogal crude needs.

text.p: Saudi Arabia will supply Portugal's state-controlled oil company Petrogal with some 40 percent of its petroleum needs under the terms of an accord that will bring Saudi Aramco in as a major shareholder, company sources said.
Under the deal, Saudi Arabia, which previously supplied about 24 percent of Petrogal's oil imports, will become the country's largest single supplier, overtaking Nigeria on 30 percent.

The Economy Ministry announced earlier on Thursday that Portugal, its Petrocontrol private sector partners, and Saudi Aramco had reached agreement in principle for the Saudis to take a 27.5 percent stake.
The state holding will drop from 55 to 45 percent while Petrocontrol's share will be reduced to 27.5 percent, the same as Aramco, from the current 45 percent.
The ministry said in its statement that Aramco will supply Petrogal-Petroleos de Portugal with its all its "sour" grade petrol needs. It gave no figures.
Company officials said that this type of petrol amounted to some 40 percent of the requirements of the company, Portugal's largest, which has the capacity to refine some 300,000 barrels per day.

Petrogal sources said that imports from Iran, which currently account for 12 percent of the company's purchases, were expected to fall because it is currently a significant supplier of the "sour" type of oil.
They gave no figures for Petrogal's overall purchases.
Although the ministry gave no financial details, company sources said the deal valued Petrogal at between 220 and 230 billion escudos ($1.3 billion).
